title: The CalCOFI 26.4-26.6 layer lost oxygen stock and gained oxygen deficit in 2009-2017
abstract: We tested whether higher oxygen deficit concentration near density 26.5 off California occurs without more column deficit. We integrated oxygen, apparent oxygen utilization (AOU) and in-situ water mass in observed CalCOFI bottle profiles. In 224 matched station-season cells at 56 core stations, 2009-2017 minus 1984-1996 oxygen stock fell by 1.51 mol/m2 (95% three-year block interval -1.68 to -1.33), and AOU stock rose by 1.96 (1.56 to 2.35). Layer AOU rose by 21.83 umol/kg. Layer thickness rose by 1.71 m and mass rose by 2.4%. The exact stock split gives +1.62 mol/m2 from AOU concentration and +0.34 from layer mass. Wider density ranges and nearshore and offshore subsets give the same stock signs. Thus layer thinning cannot explain the higher AOU concentration in this comparison. This contrasts with the published BATS sign pattern and adds mass and stock targets for ventilation models. The result is a station-grid index, not an area-integrated regional budget. Sparse bottle spacing, time limits, source disequilibrium and unmeasured boundary fluxes prevent causal attribution. Raw data remain external; code, source hashes, aggregate evidence and an audit are included.

display.caption: Matched CalCOFI density 26.4-26.6 concentration and stock changes, 2009-2017 minus 1984-1996. Bars give points; whiskers give central 95% three-year block ranges. Stock terms are exact accounting terms, not causal shares.
